preacher-ecclesiastes.name: The Preacher
preacher-ecclesiastes.role: Main speaker who examines work, pleasure, and death
preacher-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
preacher-ecclesiastes.importance: His questions test whether effort, wealth, and wisdom can secure lasting gain.
preacher-ecclesiastes.connections: The opening presents him as David’s son and a king in Jerusalem.

david.name: David
david.role: Father named in the opening description
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: The family description gives the speaker a royal setting.
david.connections: The title identifies the Preacher as his son. It does not name Solomon.

closing-writer-ecclesiastes.name: The closing writer
closing-writer-ecclesiastes.role: Voice that describes the Preacher’s teaching
closing-writer-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
closing-writer-ecclesiastes.importance: His advice closes the book with responsibility for actions.
closing-writer-ecclesiastes.connections: He praises the Preacher’s careful words and urges obedience to God.

solitary-worker-ecclesiastes.name: The solitary worker
solitary-worker-ecclesiastes.role: Worker with no son or brother
solitary-worker-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
solitary-worker-ecclesiastes.importance: His question shows how gathering wealth can replace enjoyment and companionship.
solitary-worker-ecclesiastes.connections: He keeps working and seeking wealth without asking whom the work serves.

young-king-ecclesiastes.name: The wise youth
young-king-ecclesiastes.role: Poor young man in the example of changing rulers
young-king-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
young-king-ecclesiastes.importance: His success still cannot secure the praise of later generations.
young-king-ecclesiastes.connections: The account describes him leaving prison and gaining rule.

old-king-ecclesiastes.name: The old king
old-king-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
old-king-ecclesiastes.importance: Refusing to listen makes his age and rank poor guides to wisdom.
old-king-ecclesiastes.connections: The Preacher compares him unfavorably with a poor, wise youth.

poor-rescuer-ecclesiastes.name: The poor rescuer
poor-rescuer-ecclesiastes.role: Wise man who saves a small city
poor-rescuer-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
poor-rescuer-ecclesiastes.importance: Poverty can cause people to ignore advice that already helped them.
poor-rescuer-ecclesiastes.connections: The people forget him after his wisdom delivers their city.

attacking-king-ecclesiastes.name: The attacking king
attacking-king-ecclesiastes.role: Ruler who surrounds a small city
attacking-king-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
attacking-king-ecclesiastes.importance: The example compares armed strength with advice from a person of little status.
attacking-king-ecclesiastes.connections: He builds defenses for his attack, but a poor man’s wisdom saves the city.

beloved-wife-ecclesiastes.name: The beloved wife
beloved-wife-ecclesiastes.role: Partner in the Preacher’s advice about enjoying life
beloved-wife-ecclesiastes.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
beloved-wife-ecclesiastes.importance: Shared life appears among gifts that people can enjoy during their short lives.
beloved-wife-ecclesiastes.connections: He urges a listener to live joyfully with the wife he loves.
